findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Classify the push/merge retry-loop extraction against ticket 4c4f's decision to keep it in YAML (its harness executes the block verbatim precisely because it has zero ${{ }} expressions) — either rebut that rationale or scope the loop out of this migration.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py module docstring: 'extracting the logic to a script would introduce a drift seam where the workflow's invocation of it becomes untested glue. ... Testing the YAML tests the artifact CI actually runs.'

Ticket 4c4f (closed, completion-verifier PASS) spun the push loop out of 449f and its harness drives 'the workflow's own YAML block verbatim'; the loop 'contains zero ${{ }} expressions ... so the block can be executed verbatim'.
The plan cites 449f but does not mention 4c4f or its explicit anti-extraction rationale.
findings.finding: Migrating the reconcile-bridge push/merge retry loop is a behavioral hunk that directly reverses a recently completion-verified design decision (ticket 4c4f) to keep that loop in YAML and test it verbatim; the plan neither classifies this hunk against that decision nor acknowledges it.
findings.location: Approach: 'move workflow run-block logic into Python entry points' + Scope 'run blocks -> thin invocations'
scenarios: The push retry loop is extracted to Python, and a reviewer later finds the change undoes 4c4f's deliberate keep-in-YAML decision without a recorded rebuttal.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the approach with tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py:21-27, which deliberately keeps the push-retry loop in YAML and tests it verbatim; either scope the extraction to EXCLUDE the push-retry block (extract only the expression-free classification/alert logic) or justify replacing the verbatim-YAML guard and specify how the new thin YAML invocation stays tested.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py:21-27: 'WHY THIS DRIVES THE WORKFLOW YAML DIRECTLY rather than an extracted script: the retry loop contains zero ${{ }} expressions ... so the block can be executed verbatim. Testing the YAML tests the artifact CI actually runs; extracting the logic to a script would introduce a drift seam where the workflow's invocation of it becomes untested glue.'

The test (_extract_push_block) executes the YAML push step verbatim and asserts NO ${{ }} expression was added — a standing guard that the current design is intentional and defended (bugs 4c4f, e161).

Plan Context cites '449f: 7 recommendations' and 'the raw git commit at reconcile-bridge.yml:283' as the motivation, but 449f's own analysis is what produced the verbatim-YAML test decision — the plan is unaware it is reversing a fix.
findings.finding: The plan proposes extracting the reconcile-bridge push-retry loop to a Python entry point, but the codebase already made and test-enforced the OPPOSITE decision: that this block must drive the workflow YAML directly and be tested verbatim, precisely because extraction 'would introduce a drift seam where the workflow's invocation of it becomes untested glue.'
findings.location: Approach / Scope (reconcile-bridge run blocks -> thin invocations)
scenarios: Implementer extracts the push loop to Python; the existing verbatim-YAML test either must be deleted (losing the artifact-parity guarantee) or now tests dead code, and the new thin YAML glue that invokes the script becomes untested — reintroducing exactly the drift seam the prior fix rejected.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the Scope so the push-retry/commit-back loop stays in YAML (keeping its verbatim-execution test), and target extraction at the canary's classification/alert-filing blocks and any expression-free helpers only; state explicitly why those differ from the push loop.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Identify the specific seam API that accepts the reconciler's whole-worktree commit-back (or the batch path such as batch_write_and_push), or reframe AC line 2 to a concrete mechanism, since the canonical write_and_push seam is per-ticket-event and the sidecar seams warn a whole-index commit there races normal store writes.
evidence: reconcile-bridge.yml:289-291: `git add -A; git commit -m 'chore: sync events from rebar reconciler'` — a whole-worktree commit of reconciler-produced files, not a single ticket event.
src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:557 write_and_push(tracker, ticket_id, event, ...) — the canonical seam is per-ticket-event, not a whole-worktree committer.
src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:92 / plan_review/sidecar.py:123: 'a raw git rm + whole-index commit here races normal store writes.'
reconcile-bridge.yml:272-282 comment: 'the reconciler leaves inbound events UNCOMMITTED and makes its own binding-store commit WITHOUT pushing' — a bulk commit-and-push, not an append_event write.
findings.finding: The claim that the reconcile-bridge raw git commit 'routes through the canonical write seam' is mechanism-underspecified: that step commits the reconciler's uncommitted event files plus its own binding-store commit and pushes a whole dirty worktree, which does not match the per-ticket append_event/write_and_push seam signature, and the seam's own code warns that a whole-index commit there races normal store writes.
findings.location: Approach ('the raw git commit site routes through the canonical write seam') / AC line 2
scenarios: Implementer discovers write_and_push cannot accept a whole dirty worktree, and either bends the seam (whole-index commit under the store lock, the exact race the seam docstrings warn against) or leaves a raw git commit that AC line 2 claims was removed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Engage the existing counter-prior-art (tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py's 'untested glue / drift seam' argument for testing the YAML verbatim) and justify why extraction-to-Python is preferable, or scope the push-retry block out of the migration.
evidence: Plan Approach: 'move workflow run-block logic into Python entry points ... invoked by thin YAML steps' and 'Behavior parity reviewed step-by-step'.

Existing test docstring (test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py:21-26) argues extraction is the WRONG design: the retry block 'contains zero ${{ }} expressions ... so the block can be executed verbatim' and 'extracting the logic to a script would introduce a drift seam where the workflow's invocation of it becomes untested glue.'

The YAML block encodes load-bearing, bug-cited rationale for its exact shell form: here-string classification vs pipefail/SIGPIPE (bug e161, lines 322-330), explicit refspec fetch (lines 294-301, 332-335), deliberate no-backoff CAS after clean merge (bug 4c4f, lines 353-364), and merge-not-rebase invariant I1 (lines 341-351).

The plan cites bug 449f/reconcile-bridge.yml:283 as motivation but does not name or rebut the counter-argument prior art (the existing YAML-level test) that the drift seam it warns about is exactly what extraction reintroduces.
findings.finding: The plan proposes extracting the reconcile-bridge run-blocks (including the push-retry loop) to Python without engaging existing repo prior art that explicitly argues AGAINST that extraction.
scenarios: The retry loop is ported to Python and the thin YAML invocation becomes the untested 'glue' the existing test warned about, so a future change to env/arg plumbing regresses silently.
A reviewer of the migration cannot tell whether the author considered and rejected the 'test the YAML verbatim' approach or simply overlooked it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'Alternatives / prior art' note addressing test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py's rationale: explain how the migration avoids the untested-glue drift seam (e.g. by keeping the thin YAML invocation itself under the bridge smoke suite and pinning arg/env plumbing), and confirm the bug-cited invariants (e161 pipefail classification, 4c4f no-backoff CAS, explicit refspec, merge-not-rebase I1) are preserved with equivalent unit tests. If the retry loop is genuinely better left as verbatim YAML, scope it out and migrate only the classification/alert-filing logic.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the push-loop migration with src/rebar/_store/push.py and the closed decisions in bugs 4c4f (keep-it-red, no-backoff, spend-final-merge) and the verbatim-YAML test rationale in test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py: state whether the loop is extracted at all, and if so how the CI-specific red-on-exhaustion + no-backoff semantics and the 'tests what CI runs' guarantee are preserved rather than replaced by untested invocation glue.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/push.py already implements retry (_MAX_RETRIES), the non-fast-forward classifier (_NON_FF = 'non-fast-forward|rejected|fetch first'), MERGE-not-rebase, and the explicit-refspec fetch — the exact logic in reconcile-bridge.yml:309-375.

Bug 4c4f (CLOSED, close_class=plan_defect) decision: 'KEEP IT RED' — the workflow loop MUST exit red on exhaustion and MUST re-push the final merge with NO backoff, because on an ephemeral CI runner 'NEITHER' of push.py's best-effort preconditions holds (no surviving local commits, no later fsck to surface PUSH_PENDING). push.py's contract (best-effort, never fails caller, returns None) is deliberately WRONG for the CI context.

tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py module docstring: 'WHY THIS DRIVES THE WORKFLOW YAML DIRECTLY rather than an extracted script … extracting the logic to a script would introduce a drift seam where the workflow's invocation of it becomes untested glue. The substitution guard below fails loudly if an expression is ever added inside the block.' — an explicit prior decision NOT to extract this block.
The plan's Context cites 449f and 'the raw git commit at reconcile-bridge.yml:283' but does not mention push.py, 4c4f, or the deliberate divergence/verbatim-test decision.
findings.finding: The push-retry/merge/backoff logic the plan proposes to migrate into 'tested Python' already has a canonical Python implementation (src/rebar/_store/push.py::push_tickets_branch), AND the workflow's copy deliberately diverges from it in ways a prior closed bug (4c4f) recorded as intentional — so a straight extraction/routing-through-the-seam would regress a documented decision rather than de-duplicate.
findings.location: Approach + Scope + Acceptance Criteria line 1 ('Workflow run-blocks reduced to env + single-command invocations; logic lives in tested Python')
scenarios: An implementer routes the push loop through push.py or a new extracted module and inherits push.py's best-effort-never-fail semantics, silently reverting 4c4f's 'keep it red' decision and re-opening the silent-loss failure mode on CI.

The extraction deletes or bypasses test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py's verbatim-YAML harness, replacing a test of 'what CI actually runs' with a test of an extracted function plus untested YAML glue — the exact drift seam that test was written to avoid.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the exact 'canonical seam' for the reconcile-bridge commit-back and reconcile it with the documented 'two writers, one store' boundary (event_append is the LOCAL write path; the reconciler is a separate client with its own git_adapter.commit) — confirm whether the target is the reconciler's own commit orchestration rather than event_append.write_and_push.
evidence: reconcile-bridge.yml:289-292 commits the reconciler's UNCOMMITTED inbound event files (`git add -A; git commit`), not a per-ticket local write; the step comment: 'the reconciler leaves inbound events UNCOMMITTED and makes its own binding-store commit WITHOUT pushing.'

event_append.py docstring: 'this is the LOCAL ticket-store write path. The Jira reconciler (rebar_reconciler/) is a separate *client* of this store; its inbound commit-batcher is a Jira-sync internal, NOT the general local batch-write API. Do not conflate the two.'

inbound_translate.py:9-16: '_write_event_file … writes ONE inbound event file per call under the store lock (os.replace; no git add/commit of its own) … the reconciler pass commits via its own orchestration. This is a Jira-sync internal — NOT the general local-store batch-write mechanism.'

write_and_push (event_append.py:557) takes a single `event: dict` per ticket_id — it is a per-event committer, not a mechanism to commit a batch of already-written reconciler files; the reconciler already has git_adapter.commit / commit_tree for its own commit path.
findings.finding: AC-2 says the reconcile-bridge raw git write should be 'routed through the canonical seam,' but the commit it targets writes the RECONCILER's pre-materialized inbound event files — a path the codebase explicitly documents as a separate writer that must NOT be conflated with the general local write seam (event_append.write_and_push). The plan names no specific seam and does not address this boundary.
findings.location: Approach ('the raw git commit site routes through the canonical write seam') + Acceptance Criteria line 2 ('The reconcile-bridge raw git write is routed through the canonical seam')
scenarios: An implementer wires the bridge commit-back through event_append.write_and_push (the obvious 'canonical write seam'), conflating the two-writers boundary the architecture forbids, or discovers mid-implementation that the seam's per-event API does not fit a bulk-file commit and improvises a new one.
'Canonical seam' is read differently by author and implementer (event_append vs git_adapter vs a new module), producing rework.
